subject: Targeted zone degradation — immediate reroute guidance
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Devops Team <ops@cloudway.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Targeted zone degradation — immediate reroute guidance

Hi Cloudway ops team,

We’re investigating a targeted degradation affecting a subset of instances in the us-west-2 zone that can intermittently surface as 5xx errors or slow responses for requests pinned to that zone. We’re seeing spillover into EU and APAC routing in some customer configs that prefer single-region binding.

Immediate recommended actions (minimal disruption path):
- If you use host-based routing: update your client to include the region-fallback header (x-redwood-region-preference) so we can route to nearest healthy region. Example: x-redwood-region-preference: [us-east-1, eu-west-1, apac-sin-1]
- If you pin endpoints: switch the API host to api.redwood.red{region}.fallback (see snippet attached: reroute-snippet.txt).
- For streaming jobs, reduce initial chunk size to 64 tokens to lower connection pressure while we stabilize.

We attached a short snippet and diagram for the two most common SDKs (curl and our node client). I’ll coordinate a console flag to force cross-region routing for your organization if you want us to push it on our side.

If you confirm the best option for you (client-side change or managed flag), we’ll proceed and keep you updated every 30–45 minutes until the healthy state is restored.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production workflows.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-snippet.txt (text), reroute-diagram.png (image)
From: Devops Team <ops@cloudway.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Targeted zone degradation — immediate reroute guidance

Thanks Rachel — got the note. A few quick clarifying questions: 

1) Will switching to the fallback host cause us to lose outstanding streaming sessions or in-flight requests? We have a couple long-poll inference jobs.
2) Can you confirm whether API keys will be valid across the fallback hosts or if we need to present a different header?

We’re prepared to update client-side config but want to understand if there’s a one-click flag you can flip instead (less churn on our side).

- Sofia Ramos (on-call)
Cloudway Ops

On Tue, Oct 9, 2028 at 09:12 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 09:35:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Targeted zone degradation — immediate reroute guidance

Rachel / Jonas — internal note:

- Ops: we can enable "org_force_cross_region" flag for Cloudway quickly; it will route their org to the next healthy region without requiring client changes. Side effect: small increase in median latency for some requests but prevents 5xx spikes.
- Finance: we should prep a token credit if they see capacity-related errors — propose 10% credit for the impacted window; hold off until we know duration.
- Engineering: assign a pager to look at the host selection circuit in us-west-2 and reduce the conservative health threshold temporarily.

I’ll let Rachel propose the managed flag to the customer.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success

(Forwarded message attached)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Devops Team <ops@cloudway.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Targeted zone degradation — immediate reroute guidance

Sofia — short answers and next steps: 

1) In-flight streaming sessions: switching to the fallback host will cause new connections to go to the fallback region. Active HTTP/2 streams on a single connection will continue until they naturally finish; long-running sessions may need to reconnect. We recommend draining and reconnecting long streams with a 10s backoff to avoid partial responses.
2) API keys are valid across regions; use the same key and include x-redwood-org-id header. No key rotation required.

We can enable the managed flag (org_force_cross_region) for Cloudway right now; this will be a targeted, temporary setting and reversible. If you’d like us to do it, say the word and I’ll enable it and confirm once traffic shifts.

Operational note: I’ve attached a brief diagram showing how requests will be rerouted and the expected latency delta (~+30–120ms).

Best,
Rachel

Attachments: reroute-diagram.png

On Tue, Oct 9, 2028 at 09:28 AM Devops Team <ops@cloudway.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — got the note. A few quick clarifying questions:...
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Devops Team <ops@cloudway.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident note: targeted degradation in us-west-2 — summary & next steps

Hi Sofia and Cloudway team,

Thank you for your patience while we stabilized services. Summary and follow-up items below: 

Incident summary (high level):
- Window: 2028-10-09 08:47 UTC — 2028-10-09 11:20 UTC (detected as a host health flapping issue in us-west-2).
- Root cause: a combination of an orchestration bug and a transient networking issue causing delayed health checks and a slow host eviction path.
- Impact: targeted latency spikes and 5xxs for orgs with strict regional pinning (Cloudway included).

What we did for you:
- Enabled org_force_cross_region for Cloudway at 2028-10-09 09:20 UTC, shifting traffic to nearest healthy regions with minimal changes required on your side.
- Provided reroute guidance and a small client snippet (attached).

Customer-facing action items for Redwood (owner):
- Jonas Weber: finalize and share the postmortem PDF (attached) and the editable draft for comments (postmortem-draft.docx).
- Engineering: implement a faster host-eviction path and add a canary to health-check timing by 2028-10-25.
- CS/Finance: propose a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Lauren, please coordinate pricing.

Customer action items (suggested):
- If you prefer managed routing off by default in the future, we can add an org-level toggle you control in Console.
- If you have long-lived streaming sessions, consider adding automatic reconnect logic with exponential backoff as shown in the snippet.

We’ve attached the postmortem summary and an editable draft. Please reply with any questions or edits; we’ll incorporate feedback and publish a sanitized postmortem within 48 hours.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll follow up once the engineering remediation is complete.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-summary.pdf, postmortem-draft.docx
